# PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZA – EXTENSION OF TIME LIMITS AND CLARIFICATION OF PRACTICE DIRECTION 51Y – CORONAVIRUS

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZA – EXTENSION OF TIME LIMITS AND CLARIFICATION OF PRACTICE DIRECTION 51Y – CORONAVIRUS] This Practice Direction supplements Part 51

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZA – EXTENSION OF TIME LIMITS AND CLARIFICATION OF PRACTICE DIRECTION 51Y – CORONAVIRUS] 1. This practice direction is made under rule 51.2 of the Civil Procedure Rules (“CPR”). It is intended to assess modifications to the rules and Practice Directions that may be necessary as a temporary measure during the Coronavirus pandemic to ensure that the administration of justice is carried out so as not to endanger public health. As such it

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZA – EXTENSION OF TIME LIMITS AND CLARIFICATION OF PRACTICE DIRECTION 51Y – CORONAVIRUS] (a) makes provision for parties to agree extensions of time to comply with procedural time limits in the CPR, Practice Directions and court orders; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZA – EXTENSION OF TIME LIMITS AND CLARIFICATION OF PRACTICE DIRECTION 51Y – CORONAVIRUS] (b) provides guidance to the court when considering applications for extensions of time and adjournments.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZA – EXTENSION OF TIME LIMITS AND CLARIFICATION OF PRACTICE DIRECTION 51Y – CORONAVIRUS] It further makes provision to clarify the meaning of paragraph 4 of Practice Direction 51Y. It ceases to have effect on 30 October 2020.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZA – EXTENSION OF TIME LIMITS AND CLARIFICATION OF PRACTICE DIRECTION 51Y – CORONAVIRUS] 2. During the period in which this Direction is in force CPR rule.3.8 has effect as if in substitution for the reference to 28 days there was a reference to 56 days.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZA – EXTENSION OF TIME LIMITS AND CLARIFICATION OF PRACTICE DIRECTION 51Y – CORONAVIRUS] 3. Any extension of time, whether agreed by the parties or on application by a party, beyond 56 days requires the permission of the court. An application for such permission will be considered by the court on the papers. Any order made on the papers must, on application, be reconsidered at a hearing.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZA – EXTENSION OF TIME LIMITS AND CLARIFICATION OF PRACTICE DIRECTION 51Y – CORONAVIRUS] 4. In so far as compatible with the proper administration of justice, the court will take into account the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic when considering applications for the extension of time for compliance with directions, the adjournment of hearings, and applications for relief from sanctions.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZA – EXTENSION OF TIME LIMITS AND CLARIFICATION OF PRACTICE DIRECTION 51Y – CORONAVIRUS] 5. In paragraph 4 of Practice Direction 51Y, the reference to ‘application’ in the final sentence is to be read as ‘request’. As such any person seeking permission to listen to or view a recording of a hearing is not required to make a formal application under CPR Part 23.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZA – EXTENSION OF TIME LIMITS AND CLARIFICATION OF PRACTICE DIRECTION 51Y – CORONAVIRUS] Updated: Thursday, 2 April 2020
